#### List:

- Intro
- Pharmacokinetics: ADME
- Pharmacodynamics

#### Intro:

+-------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Problems    | - Variation in threshold opioid concentration for analgesia, for resp depression   |
|             | - Variation in individual perceptions and responses to pain (psychosocial factors) |
|             | - Relatively narrow therapeutic index (e.g. fentanyl 2-5ng/mL)                     |
+-------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Implication | - Risk of underdose → pain                                                         |
|             | - Risk of overdose → sedation, respiratory depression, airway obstruction, death   |
+-------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Pharmacokinetics:

*Absorption:*

+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Oral                  | - Neonate vomiting/reflux → unreliable absorption (e.g. morphine)                 |
|                       | - Labour → ↓gastric emptying → ↓absorption rate                                   |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| IM / SC / transdermal | - ↓mAP, ↓temp → vasoconstriction → ↓skin and muscle blood flow → ↓absorption rate |
|                       |   - Risk of dose stacking → toxicity                                              |
|                       | - Pregnancy, neonate → ↑muscle and skin blood flow → ↑absorption rate             |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Epidural              | - Scarring → ↑thickness → ↓rate of onset and intensity e.g. fentanyl              |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

*Distribution:*

+----------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Cardiac output | - ↑CO → ↑Rate of distribution → ↑rate of offset of drugs with high V~DSS~ (e.g. fentanyl)                 |
+----------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Blood          | - ↓Blood volume → ↓V~DC~ most opioids → ↑acute toxicity                                                   |
|                | - ↑pH → ↑unionised % basic opioids → ↑toxicity (e.g. morphine normally 23%)                               |
|                | - ↓α~1~ acid glycoprotein → ↑% free basic drug → toxicity if high %bound and low HER (e.g. methadone)     |
|                | - ↓Albumin → same (binds opioids with lower affinity but high amount)                                     |
+----------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Tissue         | - ↑Fat mass → ↑accumulation of lipophilic drugs (e.g. fentanyl) → ↑duration of effect after long infusion |
|                | - ↑Muscle mass → ↑esterase activity → ↓remifentanil duration                                              |
+----------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Brain          | - Blood brain barrier deficiency → ↑penetration/toxicity if                                               |
|                |   - Highly ionized (e.g. morphine 77%)                                                                    |
|                |   - Hydrophilic (e.g. morphine-3-G (neurotoxicity), morphine-6-G (resp depression)                        |
|                |                                                                                                           |
|                | (immature in neonates, defective in elderly)                                                              |
+----------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

*Metabolism:*

+-----------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2D6 polymorphism                        | - Ultra-rapid: 10% Arabs, North Africans                                     |
|                                         |   - ↑Effect if activated (e.g. codeine, tramadol) → toxicity                 |
|                                         |   - ↓Effect if inactivated                                                   |
|                                         | - Intermediate or poor: 30% Hong Kong Chinese)                               |
|                                         |   - ↓Effect if activated (e.g. codeine, tramadol) → minimal analgesic effect |
|                                         |   - ↑Effect if inactivated                                                   |
+-----------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ↓Phase 1& 2 activity (if liver failure) | - ↓Clearance if metabolism-limited (e.g. methadone)                          |
+-----------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ↓Hepatic blood flow                     | - ↓Clearance if flow-limited (e.g. morphine)                                 |
|                                         |                                                                              |
| (if cirrhosis, shock)                   |                                                                              |
+-----------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

*Excretion:*

+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Renal failure | - ↓Excretion of small and/or hydrophilic drugs and metabolites → toxicity          |
|               |   - e.g. M3G (seizures, cognitive dysfunction)                                     |
|               |   - e.g. M6G (analgesia, resp depression))                                         |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Liver failure | - ↓Bile secretion → ↓excretion of large and/or lipid-soluble drugs and metabolites |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Pharmacodynamics:

+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Receptors                | - Polymorphism → ↑↓affinity for drug → ↑↓effect                                                        |
|                          | - Tolerance: beta arrestin binds to phosphorylated carboxyl terminal in ICF → downregulation → ↓effect |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Intracellular signalling | - Polymorphism → ↑↓amplification → ↑↓effect                                                            |
|                          | - Tolerance: chronic opioid use → upregulation of cAMP → ↓effect                                       |
|                          | - Opioid-induced hyperalgaesia: e.g. ↑NMDA activity                                                    |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Drug interactions        | - Additive: e.g. fentanyl + morphine                                                                   |
|                          | - Synergistic: e.g. fentanyl + midazolam → ↑↑respiratory depression                                    |
|                          |   - i.e. effect of drug A + B together \> drug A alone + drug B alone                                  |
|                          | - Antagonistic: e.g. fentanyl + naloxone                                                               |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Special physiology       | - Neonate: immature respiratory centre → ↑sensitivity                                                  |
|                          | - Elderly: ↑sensitivity (? cause)                                                                      |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Pathology                | - ↑Resp centre sensitivity → ↑opioid toxicity                                                          |
|                          |   - Sleep disordered breathing                                                                         |
|                          |   - Severe COPD                                                                                        |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Psychosocial factors     | - Differing individual perceptions of pain                                                             |
|                          |   - Mental illness: physical and psychological effects                                                 |
|                          |   - Other life stressors                                                                               |
|                          |   - Cultural differences                                                                               |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
